A type design glyph sheet for extending a Latin typeface into Devanagari. The attached type specimen is the exact style reference: match its stroke weight, low stroke contrast, humanist proportions, terminals and curve tension, as if the same type designer drew a matching Devanagari for this font family. Draw these eight Devanagari syllables in a clean grid of 4 columns and 2 rows of equal cells on a pure white background, in this order. Row one: का, कि, की, के. Row two: कं, क् (the letter ka with a visible halant stroke below it), स्त, न्त. Each syllable is written exactly as in well-set Hindi text, with its vowel sign or mark correctly attached, and the conjuncts स्त and न्त using half forms joined under one headline. Every syllable keeps its headline (shirorekha) at the same height across a row and sits on the same baseline, and the letter क is drawn identically each time. One syllable per cell, centred, with generous white space around it. Solid pure black filled shapes with clean smooth outlines, no strokes, no gradients, no shading, no texture. No labels, no Latin letters, no guide lines, no borders, no extra marks.
